cerevasc_does_not_know: ACTIVE flow regulation (current valve is passive)
Adaptive drainage based on patient state (posture, activity, sleep)
Venous pressure compensation (P_venous varies with respiration, posture)
ICP-targeted drainage (current valve opens at fixed threshold)
Closed-loop drainage control using measured P_CSF + P_venous
white_space: The eShunt currently uses a PASSIVE pressure-differential valve. It drains when P_CSF - P_venous > threshold. But P_venous varies with posture, respiration, and venous congestion. A passive valve cannot compensate for these variations. An ACTIVE/CLOSED-LOOP system that measures P_CSF and P_venous and adjusts drainage accordingly could maintain optimal ICP across all patient states.
eShunt_specific_advantage: The CSF-to-venous boundary is UNIQUE to eShunt. VP shunts drain to peritoneum (different pressure dynamics, different compensation needs). The venous boundary is MEASURABLE, MODELED, and CONTROLLABLE — making closed-loop regulation possible in a way VP shunts cannot achieve.
